items.title: 5 reasons why Europe is back on investors’ radars
items.excerpt: Key takeaways: The AI trade may be losing its gravitational pull: Even a moderation in AI spending expectations could encourage global capital to seek returns beyond US technology, with Europe a potential beneficiary. Europe has its own investment cycle: Fiscal expansion, defence spending and the push for greater self-sufficiency could unlock multi-year earnings opportunities that are less dependent on the AI buildout. The policy backdrop could turn more favourable: Potential constraints on US tariff escalation, reduced geopolitical tensions and monetary policy continuity at the ECB could improve Europe's relative investment appeal. items.title: Core PCE heats up as Q3 GDP climbs to 4.3%.

Treasury yields ease as the 5-Year falls six basis points and the 10-Year drops seven basis points, while the USD climbs against the euro, yen and pound. October headline PCE rises 0.3% on the month, while core PCE reaches 3.3% year over year and third-quarter GDP is revised up to 4.3%. Investors do not need to be early to benefit from a company's long-term success . items.title: Euro FX futures fell below 1.09 to lowest since April.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures declined sharply to start the week, sliding from a session high near 1.10 to dip below 1.09 before closing around that level. The intraday move below 1.09 marked the lowest print since April, though modest buying emerged off the lows. Renewed expectations for Federal Reserve tightening supported the U.S. dollar, adding downward pressure on the euro. As prices pressed toward year-to-date lows, implied volatility tracked by the CVOL index firmed higher. Positioning data from last week, prior to Monday's selloff, also showed speculators adding to net short positions, bringing bearish positioning to its highest level in more than 10 years.
